question.leadin: This politically-motivated event was perpetrated by activists who exited the Old South Meeting House dressed as Native Americans.
question.text: Name this event in which a group of rebellious colonists dumped over 300 chests of a certain British good into a Massachusetts harbor.
question.clue: The Beaver, Eleanor, and Dartmouth weren't allowed by Governor Thomas Hutchinson to return to England, leading to this event.

swap.leadin: Give the following about the Adams family.
swap.text: John Adams was married to this early feminist, who advised him to "remember the ladies" in one of their numerous correspondences.
swap.clue: One politician denied this woman's claims that "all men would be tyrants if they could," arguing that her requests of Congress would subject it to a "despotism of the petticoat."

question.text: de Gouges' Declaration of the Rights of Woman was a response to the Declaration of the Rights of Man, a 1789 document written in part by this French general, who had spent several years in America fighting for the colonists.
question.answerHtml: Marquis de Lafayette (accept Marie-Joseph Paul Yves Roch Gilbert du Motier)
question.clue: With the Comte de Mirabeau, this man drafted the Declaration of the Rights of Man, which was modeled after the Declaration of Independence.

swap.text: During the Revolutionary War, the Green Mountain Boys captured this fort on Lake Champlain. This fort's cannons were then transported to Boston to help siege the city.
swap.clue: This fort's location near Lake Champlain made it useful in monitoring trade routes between New York and Canada.

question.leadin: Name some European aristocrats who fought for American independence during the American Revolution.
question.text: During the revolt of the Bar Confederation, this general was accused of attempting to kidnap Stanislaw ("stah-nee-swaff") II Augustus. This general helped reorganize the American cavalry and died following the Siege of Savannah.
question.clue: With Michael Kovats, this Eastern European nobleman reformed the American cavalry during the Revolutionary War.

swap.leadin: Name some members of America's illustrious founding generation who all hail from the great Commonwealth of Virginia.
swap.text: While writing the Declaration, Jefferson 'borrowed' from this principle author the Virginia Declaration of Rights, a staunch Anti-Federalist.
swap.clue: The concepts in this politician's Fairfax Resolves influenced a document he demanded that introduced the right to bear arms.

question.leadin: Name these facts about historical figures with the last name Putnam.
question.text: Prior to founding the Ohio Company with Mannaseh Cutler, Rufus Putnam served under this general, who decisively defeated an Indian alliance led by Blue Jacket and Little Turtle at the Battle of Fallen Timbers.
question.clue: Following that victory against Blue Jacket, this man negotiated the Treaty of Greenville.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the role of playwrights in the American Revolution.
swap.text: The British playwright John Burgoyne found some success with works like The Maid of the Oaks and The Heiress, but is better known for losing this campaign against forces led by Horatio Gates and Benedict Arnold.
swap.answerHtml: Saratoga campaign [or Battles of Saratoga; accept the Battle of Freeman’s Farm or the Battle of Bemis Heights]
swap.clue: John Trumbull's painting of the end of this campaign prominently shows a cannon next to Daniel Morgan and a potentially ahistorical stars and stripes flag.

question.leadin: Name these northern battles of the American Revolution.
question.text: At this creek on the Pennsylvania-Delaware border, the British won a September 1777 battle for access to Philadelphia.
question.clue: General von Knyphausen led the flanking attack that ended this battle, which was followed by a defeat for Anthony Wayne known as the Paoli Massacre.

swap.text: The League of Armed Neutrality was used by Russia to protect shipping during this conflict. French forces under the Comte de Rochambeau helped win the Battle of Yorktown in this war.
swap.clue: The Intolerable Acts precipitated this war, which involved an early battle at Bunker Hill.

question.leadin: Identify the following about a Revolutionary War battle.
question.text: This British commander-in-chief and governor of remarked after the Red Coats' three charges up , "One more victory like that will destroy us."
question.clue: This British general's wife Margaret may have leaked his plans for a secret night march to capture Samuel Adams and John Hancock at Lexington. William Howe replaced this general after the Battle of Bunker Hill.

swap.text: Paine feuded with this Pennsylvania politician, who was known as the "Financier of the Revolution". In 1781, he became the Superintendent of Finance for the U.S. He has the same last name as the peg-legged author of the Constitution's preamble.
swap.clue: The panic of 1797 caused him to fall into debt, though the Bankruptcy Act of 1801 was written specifically to release him from prison.

question.leadin: Its namesake wrote a letter to Horatio Gates stating that, "Heaven has been determined to save your country, or a weak general and bad counselors would have ruined it."
question.text: Name this attempt to remove George Washington from his command of the Continental Army.
question.clue: Another member of this group defeated Arthur St. Clair in a Pennsylvania gubernatorial election and John Cadwalader shot this group's namesake in the mouth in a duel.

swap.leadin: While serving as the Continental Congress's envoy to France, Silas Deane used a type of this substance containing glycerine and cobalt chloride.
swap.text: Name this substance used by a group whose leader Benjamin Tallmadge used the alias "John Bolton." James Jay invented a type of this substance known as the "sympathetic stain."
swap.answerHtml: invisible ink [accept security ink; accept sympathetic ink; prompt on ink]

question.leadin: This battle was fought immediately after the victory over drunken Hessians at Trenton.
question.text: Name this New Jersey battle, a Revolutionary War victory that saw American troops spill across Quaker Bridge.
question.clue: At a critical point in this engagement, John Cadwalader arrived with militiamen to support the fleeing forces of Hugh Mercer, who the British mistook for George Washington.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the history of unicameralism in the United States.
swap.text: This document established the first unicameral legislature in the United States at the federal level. The eventual New Jersey Plan took influences from this first constitution of the United States.
swap.answerHtml: Articles of Confederation [or The Articles of Confederation and Perpetual Union]
swap.clue: The New Jersey and Virginia plans were alternatives to this document proposed at the 1787 Philadelphia Convention.

question.text: In Paris, Beaumarchais and Silas Deane encouraged this Scottish mercenary's plan to sabotage the Royal Navy dockyards in Portsmouth and Bristol by blowing them up, using flammable liquids obtained from his profession.
question.answerHtml: John the Painter [or James Aitken or Johnny Aitken; prompt on John or James]

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Daughters of Liberty.
swap.text: A nine-year-old Daughter of Liberty named Sarah, who had this given surname, gained fame by accepting tea from Loyalist governor William Franklin, then dumping it out a window. She shares this surname of French origin with the mixed-race editor of the Cherokee Phoenix newspaper.

question.leadin: In this battle, the Comte de Grasse's 24 ship west Indies fleet was reinforced after 3 indecisive days with siege guns fron Newport.
question.text: Name this battle, named the "decisive battle of the war" by Sir William James, lost by Admiral Thomas Graves.

swap.text: This employee of John Brown helped lead the raiders during the Gaspee affair. He was accused by James Wallace of burning the Gaspee.
